evidence.excerpt: CNC cutting machines incur tool travel cost that depends on both the positions and the sequencing of piece outlines on the cutting plan. This paper addresses a bi-objective nesting problem minimising material waste and total cutting-path length simultaneously. A variable neighbourhood search (VNS) algorithm alternates between three neighbourhood structures: piece translation, piece swap, and sequence reversal of a cutting-path segment. The two objectives are combined via an ε-constraint method to generate approximate Pareto fronts. Experiments on six instances from an automotive gasket manufacturer show that layouts optimised solely for material utilisation have cutting paths 18 to 34% longer than layouts optimised for path length alone. VNS generates Pareto fronts of 15 to 22 non-dominated solutions per instance in under 20 minutes. A sensitivity analysis indicates that cutting-path savings of 12% can typically be achieved with less than 1 percentage-point sacrifice in material utilisation by selecting solutions in the knee region of the Pareto front.
